sources.title: Original interview note containing the three-color ball DP problem
Structured repository question for the constrained three-color placement count
Deterministic Java validation for the exact last-two-colors DP

claims.text: The raw note defines exactly three colors (red, yellow, blue), n positions, and an explosion whenever any consecutive three balls are a permutation containing all three colors; it asks for the number of non-exploding placements and notes that a DP can derive the next state from the previous two positions.

Remembering the previous two colors is sufficient because appending one color creates exactly one new length-three window; rejecting only triples whose three colors are pairwise distinct preserves precisely the source constraint.

The exact implementation returns 1,3,9,21,51,123,297 for n=0..6 under the documented implementation boundary, agrees with an independent exhaustive enumerator for every n=0..10, and agrees with the independently derived two-state recurrence through n=200.

With exactly three fixed colors there are 9 last-two-color states and at most 27 transition attempts per length, so the running time is linear in n and the rolling DP uses constant state space apart from BigInteger magnitude.

checks: source example semantics: all six RGB permutations are forbidden

findings: The candidate preserves the raw note's actual contract: three fixed colors, n positions, and every all-distinct length-three window forbidden.
It correctly interprets '某种排列' as all six permutations rather than only the literal red-yellow-blue order.
The state keeps exactly the information needed to judge the only newly created length-three window and gives a valid transition invariant.

The Java implementation uses exact BigInteger counts because the source provides neither a numeric bound nor a modulus; n=0 is explicitly labeled as an implementation boundary rather than a source claim.
Independent exhaustive enumeration through n=10 and an independently derived aggregated-state recurrence through n=200 agree with the implementation.
The answer includes executable code, complexity, boundary cases, source ambiguity boundaries, and question-specific follow-ups.
No production experience or hidden source constraint is fabricated; required human approval remains a separate promotion gate.
